title: Phonon-Enabled Collective Strong Coupling of Color Centers in a Plasmonic Cavity
authors: Bharti Garg, Prabhdeep Singh, Masoud Taleb, Nahid Talebi
abstract: Quantum emitters in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) are promising building blocks for solid-state quantum photonics because of their bright room-temperature emission. These emitters strongly interact with lattice vibrations, which partially underpins their excitation efficiency. Here, using complementary cathodoluminescence (CL) and photoluminescence (PL) spectroscopy, we demonstrate cavity-mediated interactions between hBN quantum emitters coupled to the same plasmonic Au void cavity at the room temperature. Cathodoluminescence measurements reveal that a vibronic transition of the 443 nm emitter hybridizes with the cavity mode, giving rise to a spectrally resolved splitting, while the neighboring 537 nm emitter remains in the weak-coupling regime despite spectral overlap. The energy split of the CL peak is at the order of 36.2 meV, whereas the PL-resolved peak is approximately 24.1 meV, which is due to the collective excitations of multiple emitters per electron excitation and their mutual interactions. Maxwell-Bloch simulations reproduce the experimental spectra and identify the observed splitting as the result of cavity-induced hybridization. Excitation-dependent PL further shows that the hybridized state can be accessed through phonon-assisted excitations below the zero-phonon transition. These results demonstrate that vibronic transitions provide an effective pathway for controlling interactions between multiple quantum emitters in hybrid plasmonic nanophotonic systems.
summary: This paper investigates the strong coupling between color center quantum emitters in hBN and a plasmonic cavity. Using CL and PL spectroscopy, the authors observed spectral splitting in one emitter's vibronic transition, confirming cavity-mediated strong coupling. The results demonstrate that vibronic pathways offer a controllable mechanism for engineering interactions between multiple quantum emitters in nanoscale photonic structures.
main_problem: The study aims to demonstrate and characterize cavity-mediated strong coupling between multiple quantum emitters (color centers) embedded in a plasmonic nanophotonic cavity.
main_result: The research successfully observed spectral splitting in the emission of one emitter, confirming strong coupling via vibronic transitions, while another emitter remained in the weak-coupling regime.
method: The work combines complementary experimental techniques, including Cathodoluminescence (CL) and Photoluminescence (PL) spectroscopy, with theoretical validation using Maxwell-Bloch simulations.
model_or_system: The system involves color centers (e.g., VACD, structural defects) in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) coupled to a plasmonic gold (Au) void cavity. The interaction is modeled using cavity QED principles, focusing on the role of vibronic transitions.
key_observables: Energy splitting ($\approx 36.2 	ext{ meV}$ in CL vs. $\approx 24.1 	ext{ meV}$ in PL), spectral linewidths, and the relative coupling strength (strong vs. weak).
important_parameters: Room temperature operation, specific emitter wavelengths (443 nm, 537 nm), and the coupling energy scale relative to dissipation.
main_assumptions: The observed spectral changes are attributed to hybridization with the cavity mode, and the collective response of multiple emitters is crucial for observing the splitting.
figures_summary: Figures compare CL/PL spectra at different positions (coupled vs. uncoupled) showing the emergence of split features near the cavity resonance, and simulations confirm the hybridization mechanism.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the physical system and measurement techniques, then presenting evidence for strong coupling via spectral splitting, confirming this with simulations, and finally detailing the role of vibronic pathways in controlling these interactions.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to AMO physics and quantum optics as it experimentally realizes and models cavity QED effects using solid-state emitters, demonstrating control over coupling regimes via specific vibrational modes.

(c and d) Normalized CL spectra of the individual emitters centered at 443 nm (Emitter 1) and 537 nm (Emitter 2), with dashed lines indicating the ZPLs and their phonon sidebands. (e) CL spectrum of the cavity-coupled system, showing an energy split of the 4th vibrational resonance of Emitter 1.

Figure 2. CL response of uncoupled and cavity-coupled hBN emitters. (a) SEM and optical image of the hBN flake on an Au plasmonic void cavity. Positions 1 and 2 indicate measurements outside and above the cavity, respectively. (b,c) Angle-resolved CL map and corresponding integrated spectrum of the uncoupled emitters acquired at position 1. (d) SEM image and hyperspectral CL maps demonstrating spatial distribution of the 443 nm and 537 nm emitters within the cavity. (e,f) Angle-resolved CL map and integrated spectrum of the cavity-coupled system acquired at position 2, revealing additionally resolved vibronic transitions and the energy split around 540 nm.
